citations.narrative:
The acquisition and disposition records available for review were not current or complete. The facility did not have an
acquisition record for 11 emus born at the facility in 2025 and 5 emus born at the facility in 2026. Additionally, the facility
did not complete a record of disposition for any of the 16 emus born at the facility in the last two years.
Complete records are needed for proper management of the regulated animals at a facility and those being brokered,
acquired, held, and sold. Every exhibitor shall make, keep, and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly
disclose information concerning animals other than dogs and cats, purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, leased,
or otherwise in his or her possession or under his or her control, or which is transported, sold, euthanized, or otherwise
disposed of by that dealer or exhibitor. The records shall include any offspring born or hatched of any animal while in his
or her possession or under his or her control.
Correct by 7-July-2026 and going forward.

The facility is not reviewing the contingency plan on an annual basis. The facility’s contingency plan is dated 17-March-
2025. An annual review has not been performed and documented by the facility since the initial development of the plan
in March 2025.
Contingency plans must be in place and reviewed annually to ensure it adequately addresses the criteria listed in
paragraph (a) of this section and is still relevant to the facility and animals. The plan must provide for the humane
handling, treatment, transportation, housing, and care of their animals in the event of an emergency or disaster.
Correct by 7-July-2026.

The primary enclosure is not effectively containing the animals. During the inspection APHIS officials observed 2 rabbits
outside of their primary enclosure. One rabbit was observed wandering around a wooded area adjacent to the emu
enclosure. The second rabbit was observed laying near a gate outside of the horse barn. The animals appeared to be in
good health with no obvious signs of injury or distress at the time of inspection. When inquiring with the facility
representative about these two animals it was stated they had escaped a couple of days ago and this was the second
occurrence over the last few weeks. The facility was actively still trying to recover the animals. The facility representative
showed APHIS officials a hole that was dug by the rabbits under the fencing surrounding the primary enclosure and the
representative believed the rabbits were able to escape from this hole in both instances.
Failure to contain animals in the primary enclosure can result in distress, injury, and even death by predation. The facility
must ensure that primary enclosures shall be structurally sound and maintained in good repair to protect the rabbits from
injury, to contain them, and to keep predators out.
Correct by 7-July-2026

The outdoor housing facilities are not being adequately maintained in good repair and do not protect the animals from
injury. In the outdoor enclosure housing six goats, one sheep, and one alpaca, there is a section of metal fencing with
numerous sharp points. The sharp points are located throughout this section at the ends of fence panels and a rolled up
section in the middle of the fence line. Additionally, there is a table the animals use to climb on that has a board that is
noticeably cracked, sagging, and contains a pointed end.
Failure to maintain housing facilities in good repair could result in injury and entrapment. The facility must be constructed
of such material and of such strength as appropriate for the animals involved. Correct by ensuring outdoor housing
facilities are structurally sound and maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury.
Correct by 7-July-2026.
The exit interview was not conducted due to the lack of availability of a facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Jonathan Tomkovitch, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
